pr_body:
Today if an index is deleted during a very specific order of snapshot
finalizations then it's possible we'll miscalculate the latest shard
generations for the shards in that index, causing the deletion of a
shard-level `index-UUID` blob which prevents further snapshots of that
shard.

Closes #101029
pr_title: Fix deleting index during snapshot finalization
pr_comment: Hi @DaveCTurner, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

Ok I think that this works. If we are finalizing a snapshot then we have already computed the new shard gens, and that determines the blobs which will be deleted, so we can use them. On the failure paths if we're not in the process of finalization then we're not going to delete any shard gen blobs, so it's ok not to update the generations of any other active shard snapshots, so `ShardGenerations#EMPTY` is fine. I've been running the tests on this for a while without encountering any problems.

review_comment: I think the problem provokes without adding a new index. I also understand why you want to add it ofc, but should we do this randomly instead?
I added a comment in e4280a7f583 about why we recreate the index here.

It feels we could have a `IndexShardGenerations` class to encapsulate the list of shardGeneration so that indexing into it with shardId (which always get me think for a moment) can be hidden away. In any case, it is not part of this PR.

I think this relies on the delete index action running on the direct executor, I wonder if we can assert that the snapshot is not finalized after the deletion or something similar to catch if this should stop being executed prior to the finalization?
Yeah I suppose we might move to a different executor in future there. We can just call the `MetadataDeleteIndexService` directly, see a6025fcd8156c6e48cbda117d93e22183da9f5c8.

I think this is a behaviour change? Previously a failed snapshot can have individual shard snapshot being successful and in turn update other snapshot's shardGen assignments. This is especially true for clones since `buildGenerations` does not even check `Metadata` for clones. Since you said 

> On the failure paths if we're not in the process of finalization then we're not going to delete any shard gen blobs, it's ok not to update the generations of any other active shard snapshots, so ShardGenerations#EMPTY is fine

This change might be intentional. If that is the case, I find the other places where we pass `shardGenerations` to `handleFinalizationFailure` are a bit inconsistent. In both places, the failure occurs before the cleanup process can run. Hence we are not deleting any shard gen blobs either. So should we also use `ShardGenerations#EMPTY`?

I suspect it is not possible to observe the difference in behaviour here (except ofc that the bug is fixed 😁). It doesn't really matter which shard gen we use in these failure cases, both possible blobs are valid choices, since the snapshot itself doesn't get written to the root blob.
I'd personally prefer to have this minor consistency. But I also agree it likely won't make difference in practice.

I dug into this some more. I think we need to use the updated `shardGenerations` in the `FinalizeSnapshotContext` listener because we might have written the new root blob before failing. The other one looks like it could be either, I'm going to leave it as-is since that's the one that's had the most thorough testing. I added comments about this in 88ff699a92f.

I'm suspicious about passing the unmodified `repositoryData` into `handleFinalizationFailure` if the `FinalizeSnapshotContext` fails, because it's possible we wrote another root blob at this point so we should really throw away all our local state and start again. As things stand I suspect we will observe the new root blob some time later and incorrectly interpret this as evidence of concurrent writes, marking the repository as corrupt. But that's a question for another day I think.
